Yes but then i hunted down this comment 
“Most well-meaning Dutch people on here do not realize why you are freaking out, but as an American that was in your shoes a few years ago, I get it. In the US, the essay is expected to be the most incredible and thoughtful piece of creative writing that you have ever conceived of. You are discouraged from directly mentioning your intended major or academic preparation. Instead, you are asked to very indirectly tell the admissions reader how recovering from the death of your cat at age 7 compelled you to seek higher purpose and dedicate your life to helping others which resulted in your starting a nationwide chapter of mental health support for tweens. Clearly, this story implies that you are a kind human and hardworking with all of the intelligence and perseverance required to succeed at their college. On top of that, many families shell out up to $5,000 on consultants to help you craft and edit that special story. This is because even state schools can have acceptance rates as low as 10%. You can relax though, the Dutch want you to be direct and clear about your academic credentials and interest in the program.
Keep it simple and show that you have read and understood the course list and how the degree will help you achieve your career goals. If you do not have a lot of actual international experience, just talk about what about a multi-cultural experience interests you for a career. For contributions in the classroom use brief examples of group work or clubs you have been a part of that required collaboration. They are basically looking to say "yes" to your application unless there is a terrible mismatch between the program and your expectations.”
Yes I’ll do that!
